questions.question: An enrolled user claims to be Alice, and one test utterance is checked against her reference. Which task is this?
options: Voice conversion, rewriting another speaker
Speaker verification, a one-to-one decision
Diarization, assigning turns in a meeting
Speaker identification, a one-to-many search
questions.explanation: Verification is a one-to-one test of a claimed identity against one enrolled speaker; identification searches a bank, while diarization labels who spoke when. Identification chooses among candidate identities instead of checking one specific claim.

questions.question: What does a cosine-threshold verifier compare at inference?
options: Energy in the highest mel-frequency band
Word overlap between the reference and transcript
Similarity between enrollment and test embeddings
Duration of the test utterance against a limit
questions.explanation: The verifier embeds the enrollment and test utterances, computes their cosine similarity, and compares that score with a decision threshold. Duration may affect quality, but it is not the similarity score used for the identity decision.

questions.question: At what operating threshold is Equal Error Rate defined?
options: The point where every impostor trial is rejected
The point where cosine similarity equals zero
The point where false accepts equal false rejects
The point where all same-speaker trials pass
questions.explanation: EER is the operating threshold at the crossover where False Accept Rate equals False Reject Rate. The “every impostor trial is rejected” option describes a zero-FAR goal, not equal false-accept and false-reject rates.

questions.question: How should enrollment embeddings be formed for a robust ECAPA setup in the lesson?
options: Concatenate raw waveforms before cosine scoring
Average embeddings from several clean samples
Choose the highest-scoring test utterance as reference
Use one noisy sample as the sole reference
questions.explanation: Averaging three to five clean enrollment embeddings stabilizes the reference voice representation across samples. A noisy sample can distort the anchor, while a selected test utterance would leak evaluation data into enrollment.

questions.question: A verifier was tuned on web-video speech but now receives phone calls. What should be changed before launch?
options: Keep the threshold because cosine is channel independent
Report only the model’s published benchmark EER
Evaluate and tune the threshold on target-channel data
Replace the embedding with a transcript similarity score
questions.explanation: Phone audio differs from web-video training audio, so evaluate and tune the threshold on held-out phone recordings before launch. Cosine scoring does not remove channel shift; a published VoxCeleb EER does not calibrate phone-call errors.

questions.question: A meeting system must label which speaker talked during each interval. Which sequence matches the lesson’s diarization pipeline?
options: Transcribe, synthesize, watermark, then compare speakers
Enroll, verify, translate, then compute word error
VAD, segment, embed, cluster, then smooth boundaries
Classify, pool MFCCs, then decode mel frames
questions.explanation: Diarization finds speech regions, segments them, embeds each segment, clusters embeddings by speaker, and smooths boundaries over time. Enrollment verification checks a single identity claim, not speaker turns and clusters throughout a meeting.
